preconditions.description: The dimensions n and m are between 3 and 30, and the number of copies k is between 0 and 100.
The input contains exactly k+1 pictures.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in '01' for c in row) for pic in pictures for row in pic)
preconditions.description: Every cell in every picture is either '0' or '1'.

preconditions.expression: all(len(pic) == n and all(len(row) == m for row in pic) for pic in pictures)
preconditions.description: Every picture has exactly n rows and m columns.
A valid sequence of operations exists that transforms the initial picture into the set of given pictures.

postconditions.description: The output initial_index is a valid 1-based index of one of the input pictures.
The number of operation lines matches the integer q printed.

postconditions.expression: all(op_type in [1, 2] for op_type, *args in operations)
postconditions.description: Every operation is of type 1 (recolor) or type 2 (copy).

postconditions.expression: all(2 <= x <= n - 1 and 2 <= y <= m - 1 for op in operations if op[0] == 1)
postconditions.description: For every recolor operation, the coordinates (x, y) are strictly inside the borders.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= i <= k + 1 for op in operations if op[0] == 2)
postconditions.description: For every copy operation, the target index i is a valid picture index.

postconditions.expression: set([initial_index] + [op[1] for op in operations if op[0] == 2]) == set(range(1, k + 2))
postconditions.description: Every picture index from 1 to k+1 appears exactly once: either as the initial picture or as the target of a copy operation.

Simulating the operations starting from the picture at initial_index produces a state where, after each copy operation '2 i', the current picture matches the input picture at index i, and all recolor operations are valid (cell surrounded by opposite colors).
